title: Frontier competence at a biological-order power budget

concept.text: The proposed innovation is a learning and inference paradigm that delivers competence comparable to a named frontier AI model while using whole-system electrical power on the order of a human brain’s approximately 20-watt budget. The target covers both sustained inference and the training run that produced the model. A proposed operational ceiling is 100 watts for each, subject to explicit requirements for training time, inference throughput, latency, and competence. This is a target capability, not an achievement established by the supplied evidence.

The biological comparison motivates the power scale rather than prescribing an architecture or asserting that brains and AI systems perform equivalent work. Balasubramanian’s brain-energy commentary emphasizes the importance of communication costs, while Carlsmith’s computational estimates depend on having suitable software. Together, these perspectives explain why reducing nominal arithmetic operations alone would not establish the proposed capability.

Scope synthesis: the central advance belongs here when changes to learning or inference enable the joint competence-and-power result. Semiconductor manufacturing improvements alone fall outside this machine-learning concept. Learning rules, architectures, quantization, routing, and sparsity could contribute, but their names or operation counts do not establish completion; the resulting system must meet the measured capability and power requirements.

significance.text: The scale of the ambition is illustrated by You and Owen’s August 2025 report that individual frontier training runs exceeded 100 megawatts, with power requirements growing over preceding years. Inference adds a recurring cost after training, and their contemporary estimate assigned roughly equal shares of AI power demand to training, experiments, and inference. These are dated reports and estimates rather than measurements of the AI sector in November 2026.

Conditional synthesis: matching a named frontier baseline within a whole-system 100-watt budget, at useful registered training times and serving rates, would remove power-station-scale supply requirements for the demonstrated training run and serving workload. Achieving this jointly for learning and use would be a substantial enabling advance: a system would acquire and exercise broad competence under a radically smaller power constraint, rather than merely make one narrow task cheaper.

Conditional downstream possibilities include operating capable systems in places with limited electrical supply and making local deployment more practical. Phone or drone deployment would still require sufficient memory capacity, bandwidth, latency, cooling, and integration with the device. A low power draw also does not by itself establish low lifetime energy: energy depends on duration. Nor does efficiency guarantee lower aggregate electricity demand, because the number and intensity of uses could change.

The brain analogy has an important limit. An approximately 20-watt biological budget demonstrates an inspiring reference point for flexible behavior, but it is not a benchmark-normalized comparison with a frontier model. Estimates of artificial computation sufficient to match brain task performance are uncertain and depend on software; they are neither measured brain FLOP/s nor evidence that the same training histories, workloads, or capabilities have been compared.

missing_breakthrough.text: The target capability is to preserve frontier-comparable competence while bringing both model formation and sustained use into a biological-order whole-system power envelope. Engineering synthesis: the challenge is joint optimization of learning effectiveness, computation, memory access, communication, and useful speed. Lowering watts by allowing training to take arbitrarily long, or by serving queries at an impractically low rate, would not establish the intended practical advance.

Communication is a concrete reason that arithmetic efficiency is insufficient. Balasubramanian reports Levy and Calvert’s estimate that communication consumes about 35 times more power than computation under their cortical accounting definitions. That ratio is specific to the biological model and its accounting assumptions; it cannot be transferred directly to frontier AI hardware. It nevertheless motivates examining where information is stored and moved, rather than treating floating-point operations as a complete resource budget.

Engineering synthesis: a convincing solution must retain broad competence while reducing the combined cost of obtaining it and using it. It must accommodate model state and intermediate information within the measured system, avoid concealing substantial work in external services, and distinguish low-power adaptation of an inherited model from low-power training of the model itself. The supplied evidence does not identify a particular learning rule or substrate that resolves these barriers.

current_state.text: Balasubramanian’s PNAS commentary, published on 2 August 2021, reports an approximately 20-watt whole-brain energy budget. It describes about 3 watts for cortical gray matter out of approximately 17–20 watts inferred from whole-brain glucose uptake, and reports the roughly 35-fold communication-to-computation power ratio under Levy and Calvert’s accounting. These are biological energy estimates with particular definitions, not measurements of frontier AI or a demonstration of equivalent computational work.

Joseph Carlsmith’s report of 11 September 2020 treats mechanistic estimates spanning 10^13–10^17 FLOP/s as plausible and stresses that sufficient computational capacity would still require suitable software, which may be very difficult to create. These are uncertain estimates of artificial resources that might suffice for brain-level task performance, not a measured throughput of the brain or a completed brain emulation.

Access to the Carlsmith report was partial: the supplied review says the retained excerpt does not reach the specific 10^15 FLOP/s sufficiency conclusion, the assessment concerning requirements above 10^21 FLOP/s, or several personal and resource caveats attributed to him in the earlier research. Those precise attributions remain unverified here rather than disproved. Separate documents grouped under the report’s source-index entry cannot establish its missing wording, and an uninspected figure cannot fill the gap.

You and Owen’s Epoch AI post of 11 August 2025 reports frontier training runs exceeding 100 MW and historical growth in training power of approximately 2.2 times per year. It projects individual runs reaching 4–16 GW by 2030 and estimates a roughly equal contemporary split among training, experiments, and inference. The 2030 range is a projection, and none of these statements is a November 2026 measurement. The reviewed post does not expose the underlying measurement methods. Its individual-run figures must also be distinguished from facility capacity; a facility-capacity chart alone does not establish the power consumed by one training run.

For scale, dividing the reported reference value of 100 MW by the approximately 20 W brain budget gives 5×10^6. This is arithmetic comparing two reported power figures, not a measured efficiency ratio for equal cognitive work. It compares neither total training energy nor lifetime energy, and the biological metabolic estimate and electrical system measurement have different accounting boundaries.

Luccioni, Jernite, and Strubell’s Power Hungry Processing, published at ACM FAccT 2024 and available in an arXiv version revised on 15 October 2024, reports mean energy use of 0.002 kWh per 1,000 text-classification inferences and 2.907 kWh per 1,000 image-generation inferences. The experiments used one active A100 GPU on an eight-GPU node, ran sequentially without batching, and used CodeCarbon accounting that included the other GPUs’ idle power. These details materially affect how the figures should be interpreted.

That study found substantial energy differences between general-purpose generative systems and task-specific systems across its tested tasks and architectures, with smaller differences for some tasks such as summarization. The findings should not be generalized into a universal orders-of-magnitude penalty. Its models do not establish November 2026 frontier-equivalent competence, and energy per 1,000 queries is not a continuous watt draw without a workload duration. Although the initial research described later HTML truncation, the supplied review reports full retained text and supports these table and methods details without relying on uninspected figures.

Evidence-coverage synthesis: the supplied material identifies no measured demonstration meeting the proposed joint training-and-inference criterion. However, it contains no fresh search record sufficient to establish that no qualifying result existed as of 1 November 2026. The historical motivation and dated experiments therefore support the importance of the target without settling its present-day open status.

completion_criteria.text: Proposed demonstration: name and date a frontier baseline, pre-register a sufficiently broad task suite, and specify an allowable competence gap. Register the inference workload, throughput, latency, and acceptable training completion time before testing. Report task-level results as well as aggregate performance so that low scores on important capabilities are visible. A finite suite establishes demonstrated breadth under its conditions, not literal universality.
completion_criteria.label: Preregister frontier comparison requirements and report task-level competence

completion_criteria.text: Proposed power criterion: require at most 100 watts of whole-system wall-plug power during both the training run and sustained inference while meeting the registered competence and timing requirements. This ceiling is an author-proposed factor of five above the approximately 20-watt biological reference, not an established scientific standard. Before the experiment, specify whether the ceiling governs peak power or an average, define any averaging windows, and report both averages and excursions.
completion_criteria.label: Training and inference satisfy registered requirements within 100 watts

completion_criteria.text: Proposed accounting boundary: measure power throughout training and the sustained serving test, and disclose training duration and total energy. Define how processors, memory, storage, interconnects, host equipment, power conversion, and cooling enter the system boundary. Disclose inherited pretrained components, teacher models, externally supplied computation, and remote services, with their contributions accounted for or explicitly excluded from the scope of the claim. Low-power fine-tuning of an expensively pretrained model would establish a narrower result than low-power training of the model that supplies the demonstrated competence.
completion_criteria.label: Report full resource costs and inherited computation accounting boundaries

completion_criteria.text: Proposed reproducibility requirement: provide the model and implementation details, hardware configuration, task protocol, timing records, power traces, and measurement uncertainties needed for independent reproduction. Repeated runs and an independent replication should recover the joint competence, power, and speed result. Practical claims should remain bounded by the tested workloads, model scale, memory requirements, ambient conditions, and serving rates.
completion_criteria.label: Independent replication recovers joint competence, power, and speed

completion_criteria.text: Proposed interpretation: inference-only success is an important partial achievement but leaves the training requirement unmet. A quantized model that fails the registered competence gap also falls short. Conversely, a method should not be rejected solely because it uses quantization, routing, sparsity, or familiar components if its learning or inference advance actually satisfies the joint criterion. Edge-device suitability and lower lifetime energy require their own measurements.
completion_criteria.label: Judge training and inference by joint success, regardless of components

related_concepts.text: Roster synthesis: MLC-05, Local credit assignment that matches backpropagation at scale, concerns how learning signals are assigned. It could contribute to an efficient learning system, but the supplied evidence does not establish that it unlocks a particular substrate or the required power budget. MLC-11 concerns the measured competence-and-power outcome; success on either entry would not automatically establish the other.

Roster synthesis: MLC-02, Domain learning at a human experience budget, constrains the experience needed to learn, whereas MLC-11 constrains electrical power at declared speeds. MLC-03, Cumulative learning without forgetting or loss of plasticity, concerns retaining the ability to learn over time. Both could reduce repeated work in a future efficient system, but neither implies a biological-order power budget, and a low-power system need not solve either learning problem.

Roster synthesis: MLC-01, A predictive theory of what deep networks learn, and MLC-06, Algorithmic legibility sufficient to verify and edit a model, could help identify efficient representations or unnecessary computation. Their defining advances are explanatory prediction and inspectable, editable mechanisms, respectively. MLC-11 requires a physical resource result and does not itself supply either theoretical understanding or model legibility.

Roster synthesis: MLC-04, World models that survive novel interventions, and MLC-09, Skill learning from scarce, irreversible, real-world outcomes, address the quality of causal generalization and learning from consequential experience. Efficient operation could make such systems easier to deploy, but a low power draw establishes neither intervention-faithful prediction nor effective real-world credit assignment.

Roster synthesis: MLC-07, Open-ended curricula that create externally verified new competencies, and MLC-08, Discovery of new empirical laws, confirmed by experiment, concern the production and validation of new capabilities or scientific knowledge. Lower power could make repeated learning and discovery attempts more affordable, but MLC-11 measures competence against a declared baseline rather than establishing open-ended progress or a confirmed scientific discovery.

Roster synthesis: MLC-10, Non-vacuous behavioral certificates at frontier scale, requires checked behavioral properties on a declared domain. MLC-11 requires measured power and competence. Neither energy efficiency nor frontier benchmark performance supplies a behavioral certificate, and a certificate does not imply efficient training or serving. These entries remain distinct even if one system eventually satisfies both.

change_log.change: Preserved MLC-11 and its title while expressing the innovation as a target capability.
change_log.reason: The evidence motivates the concept but does not establish either achievement or present-day non-demonstration.

change_log.change: Separated whole-system power, total energy, competence, training duration, and serving rate.
change_log.reason: A low wattage alone can conceal impractical runtimes and does not establish lifetime energy savings.

change_log.change: Retained the biological figures and qualified the 35-fold communication ratio by its accounting framework.
change_log.reason: The commentary supports the reported estimates, but the ratio is not universal or directly transferable to AI hardware.

change_log.change: Retained Carlsmith’s supported 10^13–10^17 FLOP/s range and software condition while qualifying the additional attributions.
change_log.reason: The retained excerpt does not verify the precise 10^15 and 10^21 statements or several associated caveats; missing coverage is not a contradiction.

change_log.change: Dated the Epoch power claims, separated forecasts from observations, and preserved the 5×10^6 calculation with its limits.
change_log.reason: August 2025 reports and a 2030 projection cannot be presented as November 2026 measurements or equal-work efficiency comparisons.

change_log.change: Specified the inference study’s 2.907 kWh image-generation mean and added batching, active-GPU, and idle-power context.
change_log.reason: The reviewed table and methods support these details, which materially constrain comparisons and generalization.

change_log.change: Used the review’s fuller inference-paper coverage while retaining the Carlsmith access limitation.
change_log.reason: Extraction limitations differ by source; the initial research’s later HTML truncation does not invalidate details subsequently supported by the supplied review.

change_log.change: Expanded the proposed completion protocol to cover timing, accounting boundaries, inherited computation, and independent replication.
change_log.reason: These refinements make the joint capability assessable without turning proposed thresholds into published standards.

change_log.change: Qualified edge deployment and aggregate electricity savings, and removed the asserted MLC-05 substrate consequence.
change_log.reason: These consequences require additional evidence beyond the proposed power result.

change_log.change: Explained relationships with every other supplied roster entry as labeled synthesis.
change_log.reason: The concepts have useful overlaps but distinct completion conditions, and the supplied evidence does not establish causal dependencies among them.

unresolved_issues: Whether a qualifying demonstration existed as of 1 November 2026 remains unresolved because the supplied freshness record is empty.
The precise Carlsmith attributions concerning 10^15 FLOP/s, requirements above 10^21 FLOP/s, personal caveats, and memory, bandwidth, and training costs remain unverified in the retained excerpt.

The Epoch post’s underlying measurement methods and the comparability of its reported training-run power boundaries are not exposed in the reviewed artifact; the linked EPRI PDF was not inspected in the supplied research.

A concrete demonstration still needs a named frontier baseline, competence gap, task suite, training-time limit, serving requirements, peak-versus-average power rule, and complete accounting boundary.
How inherited pretraining, teacher computation, development experiments, and external services should count toward a full training claim remains to be specified.
The supplied material does not establish a specific causal relationship between MLC-05 local credit assignment and achievement of the MLC-11 power budget.
